steps: Open http://localhost:3010/#/ at 1000px, enter a name, Tab to a section, Enter, Tab to Start quiz, Enter
On a multiple-choice question press 'a' then Enter (feedback 'Not quite' appears with a 'Show me the essentials' button)
Tab until 'Show me the essentials' has the focus ring, press Enter
Separately: on a worked problem press Ctrl+Enter to reveal the model answer, Tab to 'I got it', press Enter
Separately: Tab to the 'Quit to chapters' link (or the nav 'Progress' link) on any quiz page and press Enter
expected: Enter activates the focused control: the essentials panel expands; 'I got it' records the self-grade; the link navigates.
actual: The quiz's global Enter shortcut wins over the focused element. Enter on 'Show me the essentials' skipped to the next question instead (the essentials for that miss are lost); Enter on the focused 'I got it' does nothing (only Space works); Enter on the focused 'Quit to chapters' link and on the nav 'Progress' link does nothing (URL unchanged). A keyboard-only learner cannot open the essentials, and gets stuck on every worked problem unless they guess Space.

steps: Open http://localhost:3010/#/ at width 400
Scroll down to the chapter list
Read document.documentElement.scrollWidth
expected: The page fits the phone width (scrollWidth 400) and each section row shows its title and status badge.
actual: scrollWidth is 625 on the home page (before and after choosing a learner). The chapter cards are 608px wide because section titles do not wrap; the page scrolls sideways, the header/hero look misaligned when panned, and every 'not started'/mastery badge sits off-screen to the right. Chapter, section, quiz, score, review, progress and about pages all fit (scrollWidth 400) - only the home page overflows.

steps: Open http://localhost:3010/#/ in a browser, type 'Persist Tester', Start
Take a 5-question quiz to the score page; open Progress (shows the quiz and 5 mistakes)
Open a different browser (or clear site data) on the same URL, type the same name 'Persist Tester', Start
Open Progress and Review
expected: The home page says 'Progress and mistakes are saved on the server under your name' and About says 'you can come back on another device', so the second browser should show the quiz and open mistakes.
actual: Second browser shows 'No quizzes yet', 'No mistakes recorded' and 'no open mistakes'. Everything is stored only in this browser's localStorage (key stats-profile:<name-id>); no request other than the page and the Google Fonts stylesheet is ever made, so nothing reaches a server. A learner who studies on the phone and then opens the laptop loses all progress and mistakes, contrary to what the app promises.

steps: Start any quiz containing worked problems at 1000px (e.g. section 1.2 with worked problems 'only')
On the worked problem the workspace textarea is auto-focused and the hint reads 'Press Enter to see the model answer'
Type a line and press Enter
expected: Either Enter reveals the model answer as the hint says, or the hint names the key that actually does it.
actual: Enter inserts a newline in the workspace (the hint is wrong while the workspace has focus, which is the default state). The model answer is revealed by Ctrl+Enter, or by Tab then Enter on the button, and neither is mentioned anywhere. Typing option letters (a, t, f, b) into the workspace is correctly not hijacked.

steps: Start a quiz at 1000px, choose an option with a letter key, press Enter
Inspect document.activeElement and the key-hint text after feedback appears; repeat after 'I got it' on a worked problem
expected: Focus moves to the feedback or the 'Next question' button, and a hint says how to continue.
actual: After every check and after every self-grade, focus is dropped to <body> and the key-hint area is empty; nothing on screen says Enter advances (it does, via the global shortcut). Tab from there starts again at the site header. Verified there is no double-advance: Enter checks once, a second Enter advances; letter keys select without submitting; focus rings are visible (2px accent outline) on every focusable control.

steps: Start a multiple-choice quiz at 400px, do not choose an option, tap 'Check answer'
At 1000px press Enter with no option chosen (multiple choice, true/false) or with an empty numeric field
expected: A message such as 'Choose an answer first', or the button disabled until an answer exists.
actual: Nothing happens at all - no message, no focus change, the button stays enabled. On a phone the tap is silently ignored.

steps: Open a quiz whose first question is true/false (e.g. #/quiz?scope=section&id=1.2&count=10&seed=295939&templateShare=0.4&openShare=0.3) at 1000px or 400px
Look at the True/False buttons before pressing anything
expected: Neither option looks chosen until the learner picks one.
actual: The True button is auto-focused and drawn with the same accent-coloured ring the selected state uses (selected = accent border + tint, focused = accent outline). At a glance True looks pre-selected; a learner who then presses Check gets no reaction (see check-without-answer-silent). Pressing 'f' then 't' does select correctly and the hint 'Press t or f, Enter to check' is truthful.

steps: At width 400 open a quiz with wide tables, e.g. #/quiz?scope=section&id=11.3&count=10&seed=3&templateShare=0.5&openShare=0.3 (question 2) or section 3.4 seed 42 question 6
Look at the table
expected: The table is readable: either it fits, or there is a visible cue (fade, scrollbar, 'swipe' note) that it scrolls sideways.
actual: Tables wider than the card (up to 646px) are clipped flat at the right edge with no cue; the last visible header is cut mid-word ('Hispanic/'). The table does scroll inside its own box and the page never scrolls sideways (scrollWidth stays 400), so it is usable once the learner guesses to swipe - but in the 3.4 question the column the question asks about ('Hispanic') is entirely hidden until they do.

steps: Open any page at width 400 after choosing a learner
Measure the 'switch' learner button and the header links
actual: 'switch' is 38x16px, header links are 20px tall, the count/worked-problem selects are 28px tall. None overlap and all can be hit with care; quiz options (42px), Check/Next (44px), True/False (46px) and 'I got it' (40px) are fine.
